name: FlashAttention-4: Algorithm and Kernel Pipelining Co-Design for Asymmetric Hardware Scaling
problem: FlashAttention-3's design assumed symmetric hardware scaling, but Blackwell moved the bottleneck: tensor core throughput doubles from H100 to B200 while shared-memory bandwidth, the exponential unit and other functional units scale far more slowly or not at all - so the softmax and rescaling work now dominates the non-MMA side.
mechanism: Algorithm/kernel co-design for asymmetric scaling. (1) Redesigned pipelines that exploit fully asynchronous MMA operations and larger tile sizes. (2) Software-emulated exponential and conditional softmax rescaling that moves transcendental work off the slow hardware units. (3) Uses tensor memory plus Blackwell's 2-CTA MMA mode to cut shared-memory traffic and atomic adds in the backward pass. Implemented entirely in CuTe-DSL embedded in Python rather than C++ templates.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract), measured on B200 with BF16: up to 1.3x speedup over cuDNN 9.13 and 2.7x over Triton, reaching up to 1613 TFLOPs/s (71% utilisation). Compile-time claim: 20-30x faster compilation than traditional C++ template approaches thanks to the CuTe-DSL-in-Python implementation. Baselines named explicitly (cuDNN 9.13, Triton), so the comparison is meaningful.
notes: arXiv ID 2603.05451 verified via abs-page citation_title/citation_date on 2026-10-03; title matches exactly.
